top_story.headline: Air Force seeks design-build teams for F-47 fighter campus at Nellis Air Force Base using fast-track agreements
top_story.dek: The presolicitation, updated today, uses Other Transaction Agreements rather than standard federal contracts.
paragraphs: The Air Force's 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron, working with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center, is seeking design-build teams to deliver rapid construction projects supporting the F-47 fighter mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada. The work would use a progressive design-build model, in which designer and builder work together from the start.

Any resulting agreement would be an Other Transaction Agreement under 10 U.S.C. § 2808a, a flexible deal type that sits outside the usual federal acquisition rules. The notice was first listed October 31 and updated today to add Attachment F, covering proposed construction markups and commercial pricing parameters. The three attached files have not yet been read and are queued for a later edition.

sections.headline: Army Corps of Engineers plans a $40 million to $70 million Veterans Affairs medical center build in Canandaigua, New York
paragraphs: Two new presolicitations were posted and 3 repeats were left out. The Nellis Air Force Base F-47 campus notice is today's Top Story.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers plans design-build project at the Canandaigua Veterans Affairs medical center, valued at $40 million to $70 million
meta: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District
blocks.text: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District, intends to award a firm-fixed-price design-build contract for work at the Veterans Affairs medical center in Canandaigua, New York. It will use two-phase selection, with Phase I narrowing the field to up to five firms for Phase II. No proposals are being accepted yet.
Flagged and written up: the Canandaigua notice above. The Nellis F-47 notice is the Top Story. Routine counts were not listed by agency for this type. Repeats left out: 3.

blocks.title: Air Force Arnold Engineering Development Complex seeks white papers for secure working-area trailers
meta: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Test Center
blocks.text: The Arnold Engineering Development Complex wants white papers from members of its Velocity Alliance Consortium and industry partners to design, procure, site, install and accredit temporary secure working areas that meet Intelligence Community Directive 705 standards. Requirement documents are available only by emailing a company's CAGE code to the contracting office. The one attached file has not yet been read.

sections.headline: Transportation Command seeks commercial airlines to fly passengers and government-held weapons to Wake Island and Kwajalein
paragraphs: Three new sources-sought notices were posted and 2 repeats were left out. Two flagged notices are the same market research posted under two solicitation numbers.

blocks.title: U.S. Transportation Command seeks commercial carriers for recurring Pacific passenger flights carrying government weapons and ammunition
meta: Two round trips per month on each route
blocks.text: U.S. Transportation Command is looking for approved commercial carriers (FAA Part 121 or 135) to fly passengers, baggage, government-furnished weapons and small-arms ammunition (Hazard Class 1.4S) from Honolulu to Wake Island Airfield (up to 39 passengers) and to Kwajalein Atoll (up to 12 passengers), each twice a month. A combined route is also under consideration. The notice was posted twice, under numbers TRANSCOM27C001 and TRANSCOM27C001SUB. The attached file has not yet been read.
Routine: Defense Logistics Agency Aviation, 1. Repeats left out: 2.

blocks.text: Navy Supply Systems Command Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk, solicitation N0018927QL008 (TSV4 NARR messing and modernization): the attached general specifications for overhaul of surface ships (file, posted October 19) require that "Halocarbon monitors with audible and visual alarms shall be installed to eliminate risk to personnel should a major refrigerant leak occur." sections.headline: Energy Department adds about $1.33 billion in funding to five lab and site contracts; Veterans Affairs hospital construction award tops new deals
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

19 new awards of $2 million or more (1 from the Defense Department's 90-day-delayed releases, the RTX Corporation award in today's Top Story), 10 large modifications and 2 cuts. 23 routine actions are listed, each linked, in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Richard Group LLC received a $64,910,819 new award from the Department of Veterans Affairs, signed October 30. The description reads "EHRM PITTSBURG UD," and the product category is construction of hospitals and infirmaries. The record does not spell out the project scope.

Perimeter Solutions LP had $67 million removed from a Forest Service fire retardant contract, described as "FAM RETARDANT - FULL SERVICE, 2026 IQ-NOCOMMIT," on October 15. It is a funding-only action, so it likely returns unused money; the description does not say the work was ended or reduced.
